correctness.rationale: For x∈Σ⁵ its 2-adjacent deletion shadow is the set {x₃x₄x₅,x₁x₄x₅,x₁x₂x₅,x₁x₂x₃}, of size at most four. Independent direct enumeration confirms the eight exhibited shadows have sizes (4,3,4,4,3,3,2,4), are pairwise disjoint and cover all 27 triples. A seven-word cover is the only remaining possible smaller cardinality because ceil(27/4)=7. Exhaustive bitset DFS enumerates all 3⁵=243 input words; at each state chooses an uncovered received triple, branches on *every* candidate shadow containing it with necessary remaining coverage bound u−4(r−1), memoizes (uncovered mask,r). Independent reproduction visits exactly 649 cached states and rejects seven-word covers (even without enforcing disjointness, so the rejection is stronger). Branching/pruning proof establishes that no candidate cover is missed; not a timed-out solver or heuristic census. Thus eight is optimal.
residual_risks: Only single burst of exactly two adjacent deletions; not nonadjacent deletion or general spectra.

value.rationale: The size spectrum of perfect burst-deletion codes is a canonical synchronization-coding invariant. The first small odd-alphabet length-five/two-adjacent-deletion case has genuine overlap and packing constraints, and the exact minimum eight improves the inspected nine-word ternary construction. The exhibited eight-word perfect partition plus complete seven-word exclusion is a substantive exact finite optimum, not merely a logged example or arbitrary unmotivated slice. The fact can be useful as a benchmark and boundary even without an infinite family.
residual_risks: The result is deliberately narrow; no general-q asymptotics follow.

final_claim: For Σ={0,1,2}, length-five codewords and deletion of exactly two adjacent symbols, the minimum cardinality of a perfect code (disjoint burst shadows partition all 27 received length-three strings) is exactly eight; one eight-word code is 02200, 01001, 10021, 11002, 21012, 22120, 21111, 20122.
limitations: Exactly one burst of two adjacent deletions, ternary alphabet, length five; no general spectrum computed.
